title: Hosted API bucketed usage margins & fallback costs - playbook draft
summary: Working draft: bucket-based unit economics for Hosted API. The sheet breaks usage into 6 client buckets (trial, low, steady, growth, spike, enterprise) and models per-token COGS by model family and region, plus the incremental cost of fallback paths (e.g., model downscale, cross-region routing, burst reserved instances). Goal is to produce actionable margin thresholds and automated fallback policies tied to cost buckets.
objectives: Translate observed customer usage percentiles into discrete billing/operational buckets
Estimate realistic per-token COGS per bucket accounting for batching, KV cache hit rates, and quantization profile
Model fallback cost uplift for each bucket (model substitution, cross-region, degraded-latency tiers)
Output simple decision rules: when to route to cheaper model, when to allow degraded SLO vs absorb cost
assumptions: Baseline model mix: 60% open-7B-quant, 30% 13B-fp16, 10% 70B-fp16 (weighted by recent traffic)
Average batch efficiency improves with request size: trial/low buckets assume 1.1x effective tokens/batch, steady/growth 2.3x, enterprise 3.8x
KV cache hit rates by bucket: trial 2%, low 5%, steady 12%, growth 18%, spike 6% (short-bursts), enterprise 25%
Cross-region egress adds $0.0015 per 1k tokens (regional proxy average) — conservative estimate
Quantized variant reduces GPU time per token by ~18% at cost of 0.5% quality delta for most prompts
methodology: Start with historical token-level logs (7-day p50/p90/p99) aggregated by tenant then bucketed into percentiles. Apply per-model throughput profiles from serving-runtime bench table to estimate GPU-seconds per token. Add batching and cache multipliers to estimate net GPU time, translate GPU time to $/token using regional hourly rates and amortized infra overhead. For fallback paths, apply uplift factors: model-substitution (x0.6 cost), cross-region routing (+$0.0015/1k tokens), reserved burst allocation (+20% amortized).

key_scenarios: Model-substitution policy: replace 70B with 13B-quant when p95 latency breach persists >300ms — saves ~40-60% token COGS but risks quality regressions
Cross-region failover: during regional capacity caps, route up to 12% of requests to nearest region — cost uplift depends on egress and latency SLA clauses
Burst-reserve activation: autoscale to reserved burst capacity for 10 minute windows — amortized cost higher but avoids cross-region egress
Dynamic quantization escalation for low-risk prompts (system-tagged) to reduce marginal GPU time by ~18%
recommendations: Implement bucket-aware routing rules in Console: trial/low buckets default to quantized open models; steady+enterprise allowed higher-cost models with SLA guardrails
Create per-bucket fallback cost columns in billing exports to enable attribution of uplifted COGS (helps CS conversations)
Pilot model-substitution policy for 10 enterprise customers with holdout eval prompts to measure quality drift before wider rollout
Add cross-region egress as a visible line item in cost reports; negotiate discount tiers with cloud partner when sustained cross-region traffic > 5TB/month
Add a lightweight threshold in the serving runtime to prefer cached KV responses for growth/enterprise buckets (higher cache hit targets), enable auto-warm for enterprise pinned models
sensitivity_notes: Batch factor and cache hit assumptions dominate per-token COGS. Small errors in batch factor (±10%) translate to ±7–12% cost swing per bucket.
Model mix drift (e.g., customers moving to 70B) can double COGS for spike buckets if not mitigated with substitution rules.
Cross-region egress cost is highly variable by partner and region — use monthly reconciliations to reprice buckets every 30 days.
open_questions: What is acceptable empirical quality delta for enterprise customers if we substitute 13B-quant for 70B during sustained capacity pressure?
Can billing exports be augmented to carry a 'fallback_reason' tag so CS can reconcile uplifted cost against incidents?
Do we have legal constraints for showing cross-region egress line items in invoices for certain regulated customers?
